propositions: Write-op input surfaces (transition/claim/create) are hand-mirrored across lib, CLI, and MCP adapters with no mechanical guard against parameter drift, detectable only by chance or LLM review.

The oracle implements a behavioral contract table that rows with (op, inputs, expected accept/reject, expected effect) and executes each row against all three adapters, flagging any divergence in acceptance/rejection behavior or applied effects.

MCP adapter currently does not expose force/reason/caused_by/ref parameters on transition_ticket and claim_ticket, recorded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago until those gaps are closed.

The oracle asserts runtime conditional rules (close_class required, reason required for certain bug-close operations) behaviorally across all adapters via dedicated contract rows that reject consistently.
Adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) are excluded from the contract to prevent false divergence positives and are verified by structural negative-control test.

The oracle detects convergence in-suite: a simulated _ConvergedMcpAdapter proves that closing a parameter gap flips the corresponding strict-xfail to xpass, forcing marker removal without manual intervention.
